query: In powder-vapourization (MoO3 + sulfur) CVD growth of monolayer MoS2 in a tube furnace, what do published experiments report about how the carrier-gas (Ar/N2) flow rate changes domain size, nucleation density, coverage or triangle vs other shapes? Give each study with DOI, the flow values compared, the direction and size of the effect, and whether only flow was changed. Prefer open-access papers.
answer:
## Carrier-flow comparisons in powder-source MoS₂ CVD

**The reported response is not monotonic or universal.** Two accessible Ar-flow experiments using MoO₃ and sulfur powders found that intermediate flows gave the most continuous coverage, but their optimum settings and reported size trends differ. The figures and text below distinguish a *flow-only series* from other parameters optimized elsewhere in the same study. “Coverage” means the reported substrate area covered, not necessarily uniformly monolayer material. (prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 5-9, prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 9-13, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8, prasad2206kineticsandparameters media b8a99850)

| Study and DOI | Carrier flows compared | Reported effect | Was only flow changed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Xu et al., *Materials* (2018), [10.3390/ma11060870](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma11060870)**. Atmospheric-pressure Ar; MoO₃ and S powders on SiO₂/Si. | **10, 40, 80, 120, 160, 200, 240, 280 sccm**. The prose lists through 240; the figure also includes 280. | At **10 sccm**, only nuclei were observed, at **0.0061 effective nuclei/µm²**. Density rose to **0.2912/µm² at 160 sccm**—about **48-fold higher**—where extensive joined films formed. At higher flow it fell, and morphology progressed from discontinuous film to large, then small, isolated triangles. The paper does **not** give a coverage percentage or a flow-by-flow domain-size table; its approximately **10 µm** domain-size statement is not such a table. Its characterized triangles also have **monolayer interiors but few-layer edges**. (xu2018controlofthe pages 1-3, xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8, xu2018controlofthe media 49a3244c) | **Yes, in its stated flow comparison:** samples were prepared under the same conditions with different Ar flows. Its substrate-position comparison is a *separate* experiment and must not be read as a flow series. (xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8) |
| **Prasad and Singh, accessible preprint, [10.48550/arXiv.2206.14151](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2206.14151)**. Atmospheric-pressure Ar; MoO₃ and S powders on SiO₂/Si. | **50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300 sccm**. | **50 sccm:** approximately **80 µm** crystallites and **40%** coverage. **100 sccm:** **70%** coverage; **150 sccm:** **92%** coverage, with smaller crystallites joining into a nearly continuous film. At **200–300 sccm**, crystallites became smaller and growth more discontinuous; at **300 sccm**, crystallites were as small as approximately **7 µm**. The endpoints thus differ by roughly **11-fold in size**. The authors report **triangular crystallites across their tested conditions**, not a flow-driven triangle-to-hexagon switch; they do not tabulate numerical nucleation densities or percentages for every flow. (prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 1-5, prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 9-13, prasad2206kineticsandparameters media b8a99850) | **Yes, within SET-III:** the authors specify fixed **15 mg MoO₃, 200 mg S**, **750 °C**, and **5 min** while changing Ar flow. **No, across the whole paper:** separate sets change MoO₃ and sulfur quantities; their shape and size effects should not be attributed to flow. The retrieved preprint supports these numbers; a suggested *ACS Omega* DOI, **10.1021/acsomega.2c07408**, could not be verified as the publication of this particular dataset and is therefore **not** used as its DOI here. (prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 1-5, prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 5-9, prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 9-13) |

**Additional, less directly comparable observations.** Ganger’s accessible **2019 MSc thesis, *Growth of Two-Dimensional Molybdenum Disulfide via Chemical Vapor Deposition*** reports an **Ar** comparison at **100, 200, 400, 500 sccm** in a MoO₃/S-powder setup with an upstream **PTAS seeding promoter**. Reported widths rose from **<5 µm** to **~7 µm**, **~15–20 µm**, and **up to 130 µm**, respectively; the 500-sccm growth also had more defects or uneven thickness, leading the author to prefer **400 sccm**. This is evidence that higher flow *can* enlarge apparent grown areas in a promoter-assisted geometry, not a contradiction to be averaged with the two promoter-free series. The thesis explicitly tests flow in that subsection, but also optimizes PTAS loading and growth time elsewhere, reports mixed mono-/multilayer signals, and has **no verified DOI**; the **130 µm** figure should not be presented as a verified single-crystal monolayer size. (ganger2019growthoftwodimensional pages 1-6, ganger2019growthoftwodimensional pages 81-89, ganger2019growthoftwodimensional pages 89-99)

For **N₂**, the accessible powder-source examples are **not matched growth-flow sweeps**. Mann and colleagues describe **5.0 SCFH for purging versus 0.5 SCFH during growth**, obtaining approximately **100-µm-wide monolayer film regions**, triangular peripheral islands, and mostly **3–5 µm** diffraction-imaged domains. Purge-versus-growth flow is a change of *process stage*, not evidence that lowering growth flow produced those domains. A separate N₂ optimization report says **200 sccm** yielded roughly **10 µm** isolated flakes and that settings above or below 200 worsened thickness, but does not provide the alternative flow values or a quantitative matched domain-size series; it also uses seeding promoters and jointly optimizes temperature, pressure, and time. Neither supports a quantitative Ar-versus-N₂ effect. (mann2013synthesisandcharacterization pages 17-24, hammett2017optimizinggrowthconditions pages 1-5, hammett2017optimizinggrowthconditions pages 5-10)

**Interpretation and scope.** Changing nominal flow also changes precursor transport, residence time and the local sulfur-to-molybdenum supply; a nominally flow-only sweep does **not** hold local vapor composition fixed. Xu attributes its high-flow downturn partly to insufficient sulfur vapor, while Prasad and Singh attribute their size–coverage trade-off to vapor delivery and residence time. Consequently, neither a universal “higher flow makes bigger triangles” rule nor a universal optimum sccm follows from these furnaces. Reports that vary **oxygen or hydrogen admixture, source loading, growth versus purge flow, or MoO₂ rather than MoO₃** are not interchangeable with the requested inert-carrier-flow comparison. (prasad2206kineticsandparameters pages 9-13, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8, chiawchan2021cvdsynthesisof pages 8-10, hammett2017optimizinggrowthconditions pages 5-10)
